title: U.S. stock futures sink, Nasdaq down 2% as Amazon, Intel earnings underwhelm
full_text:
Investing.com-- U.S. stock index futures fell on Thursday evening, with technology stocks set to extend losses after earnings from Amazon and Intel missed market estimates.
Nasdaq 100 Futures were the worst performers, sliding 2% to 28,975.0 points by 20:47 ET (00:47 GMT). S&P 500 Futures fell 0.8% to 7,690.25 points, while Dow Jones Futures rose 0.04% to 52,533.0 points.
Futures fell following a negative session on Wall Street, where technology remained squarely on the backfoot after disappointing earnings from Alphabet. The NASDAQ Composite slid 1.4%, pressured by a 12.6% wipeout in the Google owner.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell the least among its peers, as investors pivoted into defensive sectors like healthcare and utilities to duck the fallout from the tech rout.

Amazon, Intel slide after disappointing earnings
Amazon.com Inc (NASDAQ:AMZN) fell 6.7% in aftermarket trade, extending losses after a 4.3% drop during Thursday’s session.
The ecommerce and cloud giant missed top and bottom-line estimates with its September quarter earnings, while outsized spending on artificial intelligence also pushed the company’s free cash flow further into negative territory.

Stronger-than-expected third-quarter gross domestic product data and upbeat PCE price index data furthered bets on a December hike, with strong growth and sticky inflation seen giving the Fed more impetus to raise rates.

title: BOJ keeps interest rates steady as expected; says CPI inflation now at target
full_text:
Investing.com-- The Bank of Japan left interest rates unchanged as expected on Friday, stating that underlying consumer inflation had now reached its 2% target and was expected to remain at the level.
The BOJ left its overnight call rate at 1.25% as expected, with eight of the bank’s nine-member rate-setting board voting in favor of a hold. Board member Takata Hajime was the sole dissenter, calling for a 25 basis point hike.
The central bank largely reiterated its messaging that it will continue to raise interest rates in response to growth and inflation.

The BOJ said in a statement that underlying consumer price index inflation– which excludes volatile fresh food and energy prices– was now at a level “that is generally consistent with the price stability target of 2 percent, and is expected to remain around that level.”
Analysts at Capital Economics viewed the statement as the BOJ declaring victory in its decades-long fight against inflation, now opening the door to more interest rate hikes.
"We expect the next rate to come in December, with rates reaching 2% by mid-2027," they said in a statement.
The central bank trimmed its core CPI forecasts for the fiscal year to March 2027, now forecasting inflation in the range of 2.4% to 2.5% from an earlier range of 2.3% to 2.6%.
“There is a risk that medium- to long-term inflation expectations will rise and underlying CPI inflation will deviate upward to a level above the price stability target of 2 percent,” the BOJ said in a statement, flagging risks from rising energy prices, artificial intelligence-related demand, and a weak yen.
The BOJ also flagged an increase in the pace at which it will sell its massive holdings of exchange-traded funds, which it had earlier acquired in an effort to provide more monetary stimulus.
The BOJ will now set an annual ETF sales pace of about 860 billion yen ($5.47 billion), compared to an earlier pace of 330 billion yen, starting from January 2027.
The shift marks a further tightening in the BOJ’s monetary policy stance, as it reverses years of ultra-loose policy to curb increasingly sticky inflation.
Friday’s decision comes just hours after Tokyo CPI data-- which usually acts as a bellwether for national inflation-- remained well above the BOJ’s 2% target in October.
The BOJ remained optimistic on the Japanese economy, stating that gross domestic product will continue to expand moderately, albeit at a slower rate, in the current fiscal year.
The central bank slightly hiked its GDP growth forecast for the current year to a range of 0.7% to 0.8%, from a prior range of 0.6% to 0.7%.
The Japanese yen firmed after the BOJ’s decision, with the USD/JPY pair falling 0.2%. Japanese stocks deepened their losses, with the Nikkei 225 falling 2.3% amid a persistent rout in technology stocks.

title: Oil rises on prospects of fresh U.S. military action against Iran
full_text:
Investing.com-- Oil prices rose in Asian trading on Friday as the prospect of renewed U.S. military action against Iran clouded hopes for a diplomatic breakthrough, reviving concerns over supply disruptions.
As of 21:18 ET (01:18 GMT), Brent Oil Futures expiring in December rose 0.7% to $115.72 per barrel, while West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures gained 0.8% to $102.77 per barrel.
Both benchmarks were on track for a fourth consecutive monthly gain of more than 10%.

The Wall Street Journal reported on Thursday that U.S. Central Command chief Admiral Brad Cooper briefed President Donald Trump on military options for Iran at the White House on Thursday, alongside Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth and other senior officials.
The meeting covered the continuing U.S. blockade and the possibility of renewed major combat operations, the report said.
The developments have clouded hopes of a diplomatic settlement, even as Washington pursues fresh contacts with Tehran to revive negotiations aimed at ending the conflict.
U.S. Vice President JD Vance has contacted Iranian security official Mohsen Rezaei in an effort to revive negotiations, while mediators have been working on a possible framework for ending the conflict.

The market remains particularly sensitive to developments around the Strait of Hormuz, a vital shipping route for global oil supplies.
Saudi Arabia's air defences intercepted another ballistic missile launched by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi movement towards the kingdom's Eastern Province, the Saudi Press Agency reported on Thursday.
The incident followed Houthi claims of an attack on the Ras Tanura refinery this week. The continuing threats to regional energy infrastructure have helped sustain a geopolitical risk premium in oil prices.
Supply data have also supported prices. U.S. commercial crude inventories fell by 1.9 million barrels in the week ended October 23 to 410.6 million barrels, defying expectations for a modest increase, according to the Energy Information Administration.
The sustained rally has heightened concerns about the inflationary impact of expensive energy, complicating the outlook for central banks.

title: Tokyo core inflation holds above BOJ target in Oct as rate decision looms
full_text:
Investing.com-- Core consumer inflation in Tokyo slowed slightly in October but remained above the Bank of Japan's 2% target, strengthening the case for another Bank of Japan interest rate hike.
The Tokyo core consumer price index (CPI), which excludes fresh food but includes energy, rose 2.6% year-on-year, below September's 2.7% increase and in line with market expectations.
The index excluding fresh food and energy rose 2.6% annually, after a 2.9% increase in the previous month.
The data come as the BOJ concludes its two-day policy meeting on Friday. The central bank is widely expected to keep its policy rate unchanged at 1.25% after raising it in September, while maintaining the possibility of further tightening as inflation risks persist.
Tokyo inflation is closely watched as an early indicator of nationwide price trends. Persistent price pressures, driven partly by higher import costs from yen weakness and elevated energy prices amid Middle East tensions, could strengthen the case for another rate hike in December.

title: Alphabet shares tumble 10% as search unit slowdown overshadows cloud boom
full_text:
Investing.com -- Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG) shares fell by more than 10% in premarket trading on Wednesday, after the Google-parent reported third-quarter earnings below Wall Street expectations, as sluggish advertising revenue from its web-search unit overshadowed accelerating demand for artificial intelligence-enhanced services.
Google’s typically mighty ad revenue grew at its slowest pace in five quarters, exacerbating fears around the possible returns the company will eventually reap from its massive AI spending plans. In a call with investors, Google management said that while users were embracing its "AI Mode" search option, these queries have been monetized at a slower rate than traditional searches.
Group-wide earnings per share stood at $2.12, missing Wall Street consensus estimates of $3.02 by $0.90. Revenue rose 25% to $127.6 billion, compared to expectations of $127.22 billion.
CEO Sundar Pichai said Alphabet was now at a half-trillion-dollar annual revenue run rate, as AI adoption gains momentum across its businesses. Customers of Gemini Enterprise more than quadrupled their spending year over year, while more than 90% of Fortune 100 companies use the platform, Google Cloud CEO Thomas Kurian said on the earnings call.
Google Cloud revenue surged 103% to $30.7 billion, while operating income more than tripled to $11.1 billion. The division now has 18 product lines generating more than $1 billion in annual sales, Kurian said.
Pichai also highlighted progress in Google’s AI models. The company’s new Carbon model outperforms Gemini 4 Argon and is being tested with the U.S. government, with an initial rollout planned for cybersecurity partners. Meanwhile, search queries are growing at their fastest rate in five years, he said.
Yet Alphabet’s AI expansion is putting increasing pressure on cash generation. Capital expenditures reached $51.4 billion in the quarter, up from $24 billion a year earlier, bringing year-to-date spending to $132 billion. The company maintained its full-year capital expenditure forecast of $195 billion to $205 billion, broadly in line with the $202.21 billion analyst consensus.
Free cash flow subsequently fell deeper into negative territory, with spending on infrastructure, TPU inventory and an EU fine contributing to the cash outflow. Alphabet also disclosed $924 billion in future purchase commitments, underlining the scale of its obligations as it expands infrastructure to meet AI demand.
"[T]he results raised questions about whether the payoffs will come fast enough to justify the company’s soaring capex spend," analysts at Deutsche Bank said in a note.
(Scott Kanowsky contributed reporting)

title: Stocks slump, bonds leap as AI giants’ spending spooks investors
full_text:
SINGAPORE, Oct 30 (Reuters) - Tech shares slumped in Asia on Friday, while the yen rose and bonds surged toward their biggest monthly gain in nearly three years as investors scurried to safety against worries that huge and rising AI spending may not deliver sufficient returns.
Shares in Google parent Alphabet fell 12.6% on Wall Street and slid a little further after hours, to wipe out a withering $500 billion in market value, as massive AI spending turned the company’s cash flow negative.
An aftermarket plunge of 23% in Intel shares and a drop of 7% in Amazon stocks, as they too burn through cash, drove Nasdaq 100 futures down 1.4% and sent stocks of chipmakers around Asia into a tailspin.
"The market isn’t necessarily questioning whether the AI buildout can be financed," said Pepperstone analyst Chris Weston. "It’s increasingly questioning whether shareholders will earn an adequate return on the enormous capital being deployed."
Nerves were also frayed by a potentially record-breaking hack at Binance, the world’s biggest cryptocurrency exchange, which drove down bitcoin, other cryptocurrency prices and stocks including rival exchange Coinbase.
South Korea’s KOSPI slumped 5% for an October fall of more than 17%. Japan’s Nikkei fell 3%.
The Bank of Japan left interest rates on hold, which was expected and did not trigger major currency or bond moves, but Nikkei futures slipped after the BOJ announced plans to sharply accelerate exchange-traded fund sales next year.
In China, the blue chip CSI300 headed for its largest monthly fall in a decade, after nearly four months of AI stocks tanking on fears that a slowdown in demand for chips and other data centre equipment could crush revenues.
Investors’ rush into bonds was further spurred by the Federal Reserve’s Wednesday decision to keep US interest rates on hold, with no firm projection of when it might hike next.
Benchmark 10-year US Treasury yields fell by more than 7 basis points in Tokyo trade on Friday to 4.91% for a fall of some 37 bps through October — the largest one-month drop since December 2023.
Two-year yields dropped by more than 8 bps to 4.57% and Fed funds futures rallied as investors dialled back some expectations for US rate hikes. Yields fall when bond prices rise.
The risk-averse mood strengthened haven currencies such as the yen and Swiss franc, with the yen up about 0.3% at 157.20 per dollar and the franc at 0.8213 to the dollar and not far from a one-month high.
The euro inched up 0.1% to $1.1194.

title: Asian currencies mixed as dollar retreats, yen steadies ahead of BOJ decision
full_text:
The U.S. dollar index fell 0.3% to 101.76, although it remained on track for a 0.3% gain in October, marking a second consecutive monthly advance. The USD/JPY pair slipped 0.2% to 157.51, while the EUR/USD pair rose marginally by 0.1% to 1.1195 and the GBP/USD pair gained modestly to 1.3391.
The yen was on track to lose around 0.2% against the dollar this month, while the euro was heading for a 1.2% monthly decline.
Yen awaits BOJ as AI-related selling sends investors toward bonds
The BOJ is widely expected to leave its policy rate unchanged at 1.25% on Friday, despite persistent inflation pressures. Markets are looking for a relatively hawkish message on the future path of interest rates, with traders pricing in around an 80% probability of a December rate increase.
The decision follows rate holds by the Federal Reserve, ECB and RBNZ this week.
Those central banks are taking time to assess persistent inflation and tighter financial conditions, but elevated energy prices and the lack of progress toward resolving the Middle East conflict mean further tightening has not been ruled out.
The Bank of England and Reserve Bank of Australia will be in focus next week.
The yen had weakened slightly to around 157.81 per dollar in earlier trading and was on course for a monthly decline of about 0.2%, the pair was little changed over the week.
Aussie tracks inflation and producer costs ahead of RBA meeting
The Australian dollar was little changed at $0.7033, although it has gained around 1.2% this month and was 0.2% higher than Monday's close. Investors were weighing fresh producer-price data against September inflation figures and comments from RBA Governor Michele Bullock ahead of next week's policy meeting.
Australia's September CPI came in slightly above expectations, with annual inflation rising to 4.3% from 4.0% versus a 4.2% consensus, while trimmed-mean inflation increased to 3.6% from 3.5%.
Producer prices also remained firm, with final-demand PPI rising 1.1% quarter-on-quarter and 3.6% year-on-year, although the quarterly pace eased from 1.3% in June, keeping expectations of further RBA tightening alive ahead of next week's policy meeting.
Bullock told a parliamentary committee on Wednesday that inflation was likely to remain elevated for some time and could exceed the RBA's August forecasts.
The governor also said the full effects of previous rate increases had yet to work through the economy. The RBA has raised its cash rate by a cumulative 100 basis points this year.
Won volatile as AI concerns unsettle South Korean markets
The South Korean won has been particularly volatile during the recent swings in technology shares. The USD/KRW pair was down 0.11% at 1,337.82, indicating a modest recovery in the currency.
However, the pair had risen around 0.9% since Monday's close, leaving the won weaker over the week after a sharp move higher in the dollar on Wednesday.
Bank of Korea board member Hwang Kunil said the won's recent appreciation had been faster than expected and that the central bank was closely monitoring exchange-rate volatility.
Elsewhere, the USD/CNH pair was down 0.01% at 6.6550, while the USD/CNY pair fell 0.03% to 6.6591. The USD/SGD pair declined 0.11% to 1.2783, and the USD/INR pair rose 0.14% to 95.327.

title: Instant View: Analysts react to BOJ decision to keep rates steady
full_text:
Oct 30 (Reuters) - The Bank of Japan kept interest rates steady on Friday, but revised up its inflation forecast and stressed anew its readiness to continue pushing up borrowing costs to forestall mounting inflation risks.
The central bank decided to maintain its short-term policy target at 1.25% by an 8-1 vote. Board member Hajime Takata dissented to the decision.
Governor Kazuo Ueda will hold a news conference at 3:30 p.m. (0630 GMT) to explain the policy decision.
COMMENTS
KAZUTAKA MAEDA, SENIOR ECONOMIST, MEIJI YASUDA RESEARCH INSTITUTE, TOKYO:
"The outlook report suggests the BOJ has become more focused on upside risks to both inflation and economic activity as it struck a more upbeat tone on exports and capital spending driven by AI-related demand.
"Although its inflation forecasts remain broadly consistent with the 2% target, the BOJ seems increasingly conscious of the possibility that inflation could overshoot.
"Rather than sticking to the previously assumed six-month interval between hikes, it may now be contemplating increases every three months, making the December meeting a credible opportunity for the next rate hike."
DAVID CHAO, GLOBAL MARKET STRATEGIST FOR ASIA-PACIFIC, INVESCO, SINGAPORE:
"My take-away from the initial report is the hawkish outlook on inflation, which sets the stage for a potential rate hike in December... all eyes will be on Ueda during this afternoon’s press briefing and whether he will tilt hawkish or dovish and any indication on how much higher rates can go.
"The surprise news announcement is that the BOJ has decided to expedite its ETF sales, without trying to destabilise the market. While this may initially spook markets, I actually think this is a positive development since the BOJ feels confident enough with the economy and market."
SHOKI OMORI, CHIEF JAPAN FIXED INCOME STRATEGIST, DEUTSCHE SECURITIES, TOKYO:
"By judging that underlying inflation has reached 2%, the BOJ has changed what it is trying to do: it is no longer a central bank trying to get to its target, it is one trying to keep inflation from running away from it.
"That is a different reaction function, and the market should price in it as one. The 8-to-1 vote, with Takata calling for a hike, reinforces the point.
"For rates, that shifts the debate from when the next hike comes to where the policy rate stops."
MASATO KOIKE, SENIOR ECONOMIST, SOMPO INSTITUTE PLUS, TOKYO:
"The ETF was the surprise. I was a little taken aback by that, but its weight is still small, so while it may have some impact on today’s stock market, it is something that can be absorbed over the medium to long term without major disruption.
"On prices, the BOJ’s language that interest rates are broadly consistent with its outlook, together with the upgraded CPI forecasts in the Outlook Report, was largely as expected. But it allowed the BOJ to strengthen its rate-hike bias and hawkish stance more than before.
"This can be taken as a signal toward a December rate hike, in the sense that the 2% inflation target has been achieved.
"The key points to watch in Ueda’s news conference are his explanation on ETFs and his comments on the 2% target."
TOHRU SASAKI, CHIEF STRATEGIST, FUKUOKA FINANCIAL GROUP AND FORMER BOJ OFFICIAL, TOKYO:
"Speeding up ETF sales is a bit surprising. It’s unhealthy for the central bank to hold such a big amount of stocks, but I’m not sure if the timing was good in this risk-off environment. I’m a bit worried about the reaction in the Japanese stock market going forward.
"Then in terms of monetary policy, the BOJ said that the underlying CPI inflation is at a level that is generally consistent with the price stability target of 2%. They have been saying the underlying CPI is approaching the 2% target.
"So, the BOJ sounds a little bit soft, probably compared to the market expectation. In the end, this nuance of wording toward the underlying inflation and also just one dissident gives a somewhat less hawkish impression.
"Probably Ueda-san will try to drive safely, especially in regard to the stock market reaction in the afternoon. So if the stock market decline is relatively large, Ueda-san cannot be so hawkish. His tone could be a bit dovish."
HIROFUMI SUZUKI, CHIEF FX STRATEGIST, SMBC, TOKYO:
"Board member Takata dissented, but this is unlikely to be a major market catalyst. The BOJ also announced a revision to the pace of its ETF sales. However, with the disposal of its ETF holdings still expected to take 43 years, the impact on financial markets is likely to be limited.
"A significant shift from its previous assessments, however, was the BOJ’s recognition that underlying inflation, excluding temporary factors, had reached its 2% target.
"Recent developments in France and declines in US equities have contributed to a tightening of global financial conditions. USD/JPY has also responded with yen appreciation at times, leaving the BOJ under no pressure to rush into a rate hike."
MASAHIKO LOO, CHIEF FIXED INCOME STRATEGIST, STATE STREET INVESTMENT MANAGEMENT, TOKYO:
"A boring hold, but an important shift in the Outlook Report. The BOJ’s recognition that underlying inflation is now around 2% brings its assessment closer to the reality that conventional inflation measures have already been around or above target for much of the past four years.
"Taking its cue from the Fed and ECB, the BOJ has little reason to rush, particularly with US midterm elections potentially adding volatility across currencies and bonds. Ueda can stay data-dependent, keep every meeting live and preserve the next hike for around the turn of the year.
"The surprise was the acceleration in ETF disposals. Cutting the estimated unwind from 112 years to 43 years is substantial, and at least puts completion within a human investment horizon. But 43 years is still extremely gradual, with annual sales amounting to only around 0.1% of market turnover. The message is consistent with the broader normalization story: the BOJ is becoming more willing to unwind its legacy balance sheet, but remains determined to do so without disrupting markets."

title: UK house prices flat in October as rate rise bets weigh, Nationwide says
full_text:
Investing.com -- British house prices were flat in October, extending a six-month stall that has left them almost 2% below their April peak, as investors bet the Bank of England’s next move is a rate rise, mortgage lender Nationwide said on Friday.
House prices were broadly unchanged in October, while annual growth slowed to its weakest pace since January 2024, as inflation concerns and expectations of higher interest rates weighed on buyer demand, Nationwide’s house price index showed.
The seasonally adjusted monthly change was -0.0% in October, compared with a 0.3% decline in September.
The average house price, on an unadjusted basis, stood at £273,566 in October, down from £274,251 in September and £278,880 in April.
Annual house price growth slowed to 0.5% in October from 0.8% in September, marking its weakest rate since January 2024. Growth had stood at 3% in April.
The three-month-on-three-month change was -0.2% in October, compared with a decline of 0.4% in September.
“Geopolitical tensions remain high, with the conflict in the Middle East exerting upward pressure on energy prices, fanning inflation concerns,” said Nationwide Chief Economist Robert Gardner in a statement.
This had led to growing financial market expectations of Bank Rate increases, keeping upward pressure on the interest rates that influence mortgage pricing, he added.
Surveyors have reported that new buyer enquiries remain weak, while households became less optimistic in October about the economic outlook and their own financial prospects over the coming year, Gardner added.
"Forward-looking indicators suggest further softness in the near term," he said.
However, Gardner said there were reasons to expect the housing market to regain momentum once the energy price shock subsides.
Employment and real incomes remain resilient, while household debt is close to a 20-year low relative to disposable income.
He added that the improvement in housing affordability over the past two years had been only partly reversed by higher market interest rates, as income growth had significantly outpaced house price growth.

title: Eurozone growth outpaces expectations in third quarter despite inflation headwinds
full_text:
Investing.com - The Eurozone economy grew by more than anticipated in the third quarter, pointing to resilience in a 21-member currency bloc grappling with headwinds from elevated inflation and bond market ructions in France.
Gross domestic product rose by 0.4% quarter-on-quarter in the July-September period, according to preliminary flash data from Eurostat on Friday. Expansion in the economies of Germany and Spain helped to underpin activity, although Italy stagnated and France’s economy contracted.
Year-on-year, GDP stood at 1.3%, up from 1.2% in the second quarter and economists’ expectations for growth of 1.1%.
Earlier this week, the European Central Bank flagged risks to the Eurozone from energy-induced inflationary pressures, which have largely reflected the impact of oil supply constraints caused by the Iran war. Although the ECB kept interest rates unchanged on Thursday, officials are anticipated to increase borrowing costs in December, with policymakers keen to prevent the higher energy prices from bleeding into other parts of the economy.
Inflation in Spain, one of the Eurozone’s recent outperformers, eased slightly in October to an annualized rate of 4.9%, but was still relatively elevated. Price gains in France and Italy also accelerated this month.
At the same time, a surge in bond yields in France have threatened to act as a weight on the wider Eurozone. Social unrest, along with worries over France’s fiscal position, have contributed to the spike in yields, which move inversely to bond prices. French Finance Minister Rolan Lescure said on Friday that France’s economy is "at a standstill."
"The continued growth of the Eurozone economy in Q3 shows that households and businesses have not pared back their spending due to the Iran war," said Jack Allen-Reynolds, Deputy Chief Eurozone Economist at Capital Economics, in a note.
"We think the economy will continue to grow steadily in the coming quarters, but with energy prices higher than we have been assuming, the risks to our forecast are to the downside."

title: ECB policymakers bring rate hike debate into the open
full_text:
FRANKFURT, Oct 30 (Reuters) - The European Central Bank may need to raise interest rates further to counter high inflation and prevent it from spiralling into wages, ECB policymakers said on Friday, hours after the bank left rates unchanged.
The ECB debated a hike on Thursday, but ultimately unanimously decided against the move on the premise that an energy price-driven inflation surge is not yet generating dangerous second-round effects.
But commentary on Friday suggested that a hike may have only been delayed and such a move in December was on the cards.
"Monetary policy ... can and should prevent (price increases) from becoming entrenched in the expectations and behaviour of households and firms, triggering a wage-price spiral that would be costly to stop," Bank of Italy Governor Fabio Panetta said.
"With inflation set to remain above target for an extended period and risks skewed to the upside, further increases in the policy rates could prove necessary," he said in Rome.
Investors see a two-in-three chance of a hike in December, and expect almost three rate increases in the coming year on top of the two hikes earlier this year, according to LSEG data.
Martin Kocher, Austria’s central bank chief, echoed Panetta’s comments.
"If the situation does not improve in the near future, the monetary policy environment suggests a response will be necessary," Kocher said in a blog post published on Friday.
"The inflation risks have clearly increased. But neither acting prematurely nor waiting and doing nothing will ensure price stability," Kocher added.
Euro zone inflation hit 3.8% last month, nearly twice the ECB’s target, and could accelerate further in the coming months on a renewed surge in energy costs and rising food prices.
An ECB survey published on Friday suggests that inflation may accelerate this year and next by more than earlier predicted, and may not return to target until 2028.
"The risk that price increases will be faster and more sustained than projected remains significant," Estonian central bank chief Ülo Kaasik said.
"It is therefore understandable why financial markets are counting on further interest rate hikes from the European Central Bank," he said.
In a note of caution, Panetta added that the ECB should take into account the recent surge in bond yields, which is already making borrowing more expensive, when "gradually calibrating monetary policy."

title: European gas surges 40% in October on U.S.-Iran military escalation
full_text:
Investing.com — European and British natural gas benchmarks surged on Friday to levels not seen since the 2022 energy crisis, heading for monthly gains of more than 40% as reports of high-level White House briefings on military strikes against Iran stoked fears of severe supply disruptions in the Persian Gulf.
The front-month Dutch Title Transfer Facility (TTF) contract, the European wholesale benchmark, climbed 5.33% to 103.10 euros per megawatt-hour, marking a fresh four-year high. The contract has advanced 42.5% across October.
Across the Channel, the British equivalent jumped 5.5% to 256.47 pence per therm, registering a 40% gain over the month. Both contracts were on track to record their fourth consecutive monthly increase, reflecting an unrelenting upward march fueled by geopolitical conflict, naval blockades, and heightening winter supply vulnerabilities.
Bullish momentum accelerated following a report by The Wall Street Journal that U.S. Central Command chief Admiral Brad Cooper briefed President Donald Trump at the White House on Thursday on prospective military options targeting Iran.
The meeting, attended by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and other senior national security officials, reviewed the continuing U.S. naval blockade as well as preparations for potential renewed major combat operations, the newspaper reported.
Market anxiety was heightened by remarks from Trump suggesting fresh strikes could unfold following the Nov. 3 U.S. midterm elections. Asked on Wednesday whether he was considering expanding military attacks against Tehran, Trump replied: "Anything’s possible."
Traders and utilities have aggressively priced in supply risks, fearing that any widening of combat could halt liquefied natural gas (LNG) carrier traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, where tanker transit has already faced record disruptions this month.
Backchannel outreach fails to calm winter scramble
U.S. Vice President JD Vance has established direct contact with senior Iranian security official Mohsen Rezaei in an effort to explore avenues for de-escalation, people familiar with the matter told Reuters, while regional mediators continue drafting potential frameworks to end the eight-month-old conflict.
However, with gas inventories across the European Union being drawn down ahead of winter and global spot LNG cargoes commanding elevated premiums in Asia, energy traders have shown little appetite to bet on a rapid diplomatic breakthrough.

Most of the funds were swept across ten blockchains in approximately 20 minutes beginning at 20:05 UTC on Thursday, and the breach appears to have originated from a compromised laptop belonging to a Binance engineer.
The theft is roughly four times the size of the previous record, the $1.5 billion Bybit hack in February 2025, which the FBI also pinned on the same North Korean group.

Bitcoin fell to a six-week low before paring some losses, down 3.1% from Thursday’s close. Ether dropped more than 3.9% to a two-month low while BNB, Binance’s native token, lost 6.1%.
Binance co-founder Yi He said the exchange would cover "all hacking losses" and co-CEO Richard Teng told users "your money is safe."
Partners including Tether, Circle, Ripple, and Trump-backed World Liberty Financial have helped Binance locate and freeze about $3 billion of the stolen assets, and the exchange said it expects to resume withdrawals within 48 hours of Friday. title: Meta settles with teen during trial testing claims social media caused depression, eating disorders
full_text:
By Diana Novak Jones
Oct 30 (Reuters) - Meta Platforms has settled with a teen plaintiff who accused the company of designing Instagram and Facebook to be addictive, causing her mental health problems and disordered eating, attorneys for the plaintiff said on Friday.
The settlement came after jury selection began on Wednesday for a trial that was slated to test the claims of two teens, identified as S.J. and K.D.B., against Meta and Snapchat parent Snap Inc. Meta had settled with S.J. days before the trial, so Friday’s settlement with K.D.B. means the trial is expected to proceed against Snap only.
“We remain committed to improving safety for kids on social media apps and holding tech companies accountable, and we are pleased to have brought this matter to a just resolution on behalf of our client,” Emily Jeffcott, an attorney for K.D.B., said in a statement.
The trial is the second in Los Angeles state court over claims brought by young people who say they became addicted to social media after Meta, Snap, TikTok and Alphabet’s YouTube designed their platforms to encourage compulsive use.
S.J. and K.D.B. had previously settled with TikTok and YouTube.
The case was selected among the thousands of pending lawsuits as a test case, so the jury’s verdict could influence how the companies and plaintiffs resolve similar cases.
S.J., a 16-year-old girl from Illinois, and K.D.B., an 18-year-old from Mississippi, say they began using YouTube as early as age 3 and the other platforms around age 9, developing compulsive habits they blame on features such as autoplay and infinite scroll.
The companies have rejected claims their platforms were designed to addict young people, and say they have taken action to make the apps safe places for young people to express themselves.
Social media companies face thousands of lawsuits in federal and state courts by individuals, school districts, municipalities and other government entities alleging the companies knowingly sought to addict children to their platforms, contributing to a youth mental health crisis involving anxiety, depression and suicide.
In the first case to go to trial, which ended in March, a Los Angeles jury found Meta and YouTube had been negligent and awarded a young woman $6 million in damages.
The next two teens whose cases were selected for trials either settled or dropped their claims against the companies.
The first school district chosen for trial settled with all of the companies.
In August, Meta struck settlements worth up to $18 billion with nearly every state and US territory to resolve lawsuits brought by attorneys general over the platforms’ harm to teens and agreed to make changes to how Instagram and Facebook work for teens.
Earlier this month, a New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay a $25 billion penalty after a jury found the company misled Facebook users about the privacy of their data and how it handles hate speech. The company has said it will appeal.

title: Fed officials make case for rate hikes amid ongoing inflation concerns
full_text:
By Ann Saphir and Michael S. Derby
Oct 30 (Reuters) - A trio of Federal Reserve officials made the case on Friday for more interest rate increases to combat high levels of inflation, in the first round of commentary made by central bankers after this week’s monetary policy meeting that saw short-term borrowing costs left steady.
Calling the current level of price pressures and the time inflation has been above the 2% “unacceptable,” Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas President Lorie Logan said the central bank has more work to do.
“It remains clear to me, given the current outlook, that the (Federal Open Market Committee) needs to implement at least two more 25-basis-point rate increases,” Logan said in the text of a speech prepared for an event at Davidson College.
After delivering those increases, “it would make sense in my view to pause and examine economic and financial developments to determine what further action may be appropriate,” Logan said.
Logan holds a voting role on the FOMC this year and joined with her colleagues in favor of the FOMC’s decision to hold its interest rate target range steady at between 3.75% and 4%. Logan explained that not moving the target at the meeting held over Tuesday and Wednesday came amid volatile markets and gave the public time to adjust to the shift toward higher borrowing costs.
Speaking separately, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis President Alberto Musalem, who does not hold a vote on the FOMC this year, also argued for higher rates.
"Additional firming of monetary policy will be necessary, and soon," Musalem said in the text of a speech to be presented at an event held by the Shadow Open Market Committee, a group that takes stock of Fed actions and policies.
"Incremental adjustments made earlier are usually less disruptive than larger and abrupt actions taken later," he said.
Musalem said that inflation remains too high relative to the 2% target and added that it was unlikely to ease absent Fed action. He noted that monetary policy is not in a position to lower inflation at the current moment.
"I believe that monetary policy and financial conditions remain accommodative. Financial conditions tightened recently," Musalem said.
Meanwhile, Richmond Fed leader Thomas Barkin said in an interview on SiriusXM’s Business Briefing that “inflation’s high, demand is solid, unemployment is relatively low. So I think the direction of travel is pretty straightforward” for future interest rate increases.
“The question, though, is pace ... We signaled a gradual approach. Gradual makes sense when you’re not much behind the curve, where you want time to learn,” Barkin said.
MORE WORK TO DO
The officials spoke on Friday as the central bank’s so-called blackout period that limits communications around FOMC meetings ended.
Two Fed officials dissented at the gathering but in a break from what has become a common process, neither Cleveland Fed leader Beth Hammack nor Fed Governor Lisa Cook offered formal explanation Friday for why they voted in favor of a rate hike.
The Fed raised rates in September to help bring persistently high inflation pressures back to the 2% target and officials have broadly signaled they are not done, with traders and investors eyeing the December meeting as the next time to act.
After the FOMC meeting, Chairman Kevin Warsh was asked at a press conference why the Fed didn’t hike rates at this week’s gathering if it thinks inflation is too high.
“I’m encouraged by the progress we’ve made in a short period of time” on lowering inflation, Warsh said, “but if the crux of your question is, you haven’t delivered yet, you haven’t achieved price stability, you’re right about that. But we’re working on it.”
The Fed leader, who has been loath to provide guidance about the interest rate outlook, did not say what he thought the Fed would do at the Dec. 8-9 policy meeting.
Futures markets have been easing back on expectations of a December rate hike though market participants still believe an increase in short-term borrowing costs is more likely than holding steady.
Stock indexes were suffering large declines on Friday, with the Nasdaq falling to its weakest level in three months, as artificial intelligence developments rattled investors.
Adding to the uncertainty of the outlook is next Tuesday’s midterm elections in the US, which could see major advances by Democratic candidates, driven by voters who’ve shown deep discontent over inflation and the impact of President Donald Trump’s Middle East war.
The market’s worry that AI-related activity might slow could take some pressure off the Fed if realized. That’s because central bankers have for some time noted that very hot levels of technology investment have helped drive up inflation. Slower activity in that sector might help ease price pressures and reduce the need for the Fed to raise rates.

title: Global Payments jumps 12% on report of potential $40 billion buyout
full_text:
Investing.com -- Global Payments shares jumped 12% Friday after a Financial Times report that private equity firm Clayton, Dubilier & Rice is exploring a buyout of the payments processor, raising the prospect of a takeover premium after a prolonged decline in the stock.
CD&R is working with GTCR, Global Payments’ largest outside shareholder, on a potential bid, the FT reported, citing people familiar with the matter. The discussions remain ongoing, however, and may not result in a transaction.
The reported $40 billion enterprise valuation would make the potential deal one of the largest leveraged buyouts on record. Global Payments’ equity market value was approximately $23 billion Friday afternoon, while its net debt exceeds $17 billion.
No proposed purchase price or financing details have emerged. The FT reported that any transaction would likely include a premium, but the size of any potential premium remains unknown.
The prospect of a buyout comes after Global Payments shares lost significant ground following its agreement to acquire Worldpay from GTCR for more than $24 billion in 2025. The transaction, structured with cash and stock consideration, prompted investor concerns about the company’s increased debt burden, dilution and strategic direction.
GTCR received more than $14 billion in cash and approximately $10 billion in Global Payments shares, becoming the company’s largest outside shareholder. The private equity firm’s involvement in the reported buyout discussions is therefore particularly notable.
The Worldpay deal also drew activist attention from Elliott Investment Management, which subsequently took a stake in Global Payments and secured two mutually agreed-upon board appointments through a cooperation agreement.
The reported approach comes as established payment processors face competitive pressure from newer technology-focused rivals, including Adyen and Stripe.
CD&R declined to comment, while Global Payments and GTCR did not immediately respond to requests for comment, according to the FT.

title: Okta jumps after-hours following tapped inclusion in the S&P 500
full_text:

The reshuffle triggered a broader cascade across domestic equity benchmarks, elevating ophthalmic medical technology specialist Glaukos Corp (NYSE:GKOS) from the S&P SmallCap 600 to replace Okta in the S&P MidCap 400. In turn, equipment rental provider McGrath RentCorp (NASDAQ:MGRC) will take Glaukos’s vacated seat in the SmallCap 600, sending McGrath shares up 2.8% in late trade.
Separately, aerospace and defense supplier Loar Holdings LLC (NYSE:LOAR) gained 3.5% after-hours following its tapping to join the S&P SmallCap 600. title: Google weighs cybersecurity role in Pentagon’s Golden Dome project - Bloomberg
full_text:
Investing.com -- Alphabet Inc’s (NASDAQ:GOOGL) Google is in discussions with the U.S. Department of Defense to support a data-security initiative within the $185 billion Golden Dome missile defense initiative, according to reporting from Bloomberg. The prospective partnership would mark the technology giant’s first known participation in President Donald Trump’s flagship defense program, which is designed to construct an integrated, multi-layered shield spanning ground installations to orbital space assets.
The Pentagon is establishing a dedicated industry consortium tasked with safeguarding the data pipelines that feed the program’s core military command-and-control software, people familiar with the matter told Bloomberg. Discussions have centered on deploying Google’s data storage, networking, and cybersecurity infrastructure to ensure communications remain operational if adversaries compromise conventional terrestrial networks or cellular towers.
While conversations remain preliminary and subject to change, the effort is expected to involve multiple commercial partners, including Google spinoff and networking specialist Aalyria Technologies Inc. A Defense Department official told Bloomberg that while the agency evaluates early concepts, no definitive determinations have been made regarding the consortium’s formal structure or corporate roster.
The initiative would integrate into a broader command-and-control framework currently being developed by a defense-tech cohort that includes Palantir Technologies, Anduril Industries, and SpaceX. That layer seeks to unify previously siloed military hardware, radar networks, and weapons platforms across armed service branches into a cohesive operating picture.
The push highlights the Pentagon’s deliberate pivot toward multi-vendor industry alliances rather than relying on a single legacy prime contractor to manage massive defense architectures. It also underscores Google’s accelerating push into national security contracts following years of internal friction over defense-related work.
After employee demonstrations led the company to exit the Pentagon’s Project Maven artificial intelligence contract in 2018, Alphabet has systematically expanded its public-sector footprint with dedicated government units. Most recently, the company deepened that alignment in April by securing an agreement to deploy its proprietary artificial intelligence models for classified defense operations.
